Suggested Syllabus Statements on AI Use

1. AI use is allowed in the course with proper referencing.

Students are welcome to explore approved generative AI tools to seek support for their assignments or other activities. However, students should follow the “verify everything” approach to the content generated by these AI tools. These tools learned the models from the public internet, which means they may reproduce substantial text from other sources. It is the student’s responsibility to check the original sources to be sure they are not plagiarizing someone else’s work. Students should also cross-check the content and citations generated by these tools to ensure they are accurate and properly referenced.

Students should incorporate the subsequent statement in their assignments when using a Generative AI Tool: “For this assignment’s preparation, the author(s) have utilized [Generative AI Tool Name], a language model created by [Generative AI Tool Provider]. Within this assignment, the [Generative AI Tool Name] was used for purposes such as [e.g., brainstorming, grammatical correction, writing paraphrasing, citation, specific sections of the assignment].”

Updated AI Usage Guidelines

Dated January 2026
Amherst College recognizes that generative AI is rapidly reshaping the ways we learn, teach, and work, and that these tools are increasingly part of the everyday technologies we use. We encourage thoughtful, responsible exploration of AI as a way to support learning, spark innovation, and improve how we operate as a community. At the same time, we remain committed to protecting privacy, maintaining accuracy, and upholding the academic and institutional integrity that define Amherst.
These guidelines apply to all members of the Amherst community and are designed to guide responsible use while supporting the creativity and innovation that are hallmarks of the Amherst community.
Use AI Responsibly
Users are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any material they create, distribute, or rely upon that was generated or assisted by AI.
All final decisions, publications, and communications remain the responsibility of the human author or decision-maker.
Members of the community may use these tools to generate ideas, drafts, and analyses, provided that:
All data used are appropriate for public or internal sharing;

Key Takeaways for Effective Strategies on Responsible AI Usage

If a graduate student uses an AI text generator, they should:

1. Consult with professors to understand guidelines and rules on using AI in CSULB courses
2. Consider confidentiality (adjust settings to ensure confidentiality and privacy)
3. Use AI-generated information only as a starting point
4. Assess response accuracy
5. Check sources’ authenticity
6. Corroborate via lateral reading
7. Ensure sources are reputable, written by established experts, or are peer reviewed
8. Remain abreast of AI tool capabilities and limitations; these will continue to evolve
9. Consult with a librarian for help finding resources that are reputable and useful for assignments
10. Remember that the purpose of graduate school is to learn; retain your agency as a graduate scholar-researcher-
author

That said, developing AI fluency is essential. In today’s workplace, those who can use AI tools effectively stand out during the interview process and in the workforce. But your role isn’t to just use AI tools. GenAI Policy

Don’t Ignore GenAI

Don’t ignore the presence and widespread use by students of a variety of different GenAI products to generate text, code, images, CAD designs, slides, video, and audio.

Include a statement on GenAI in your syllabus

Every College of Engineering course syllabus should have a GenAI policy statement that is consistent with the learning objectives of the course. Course evaluation components should be designed to support the stated policy.

As learners, students will benefit from specific guidance for your course, not just a general reference to following the Academic Integrity Code.
